intro_html: All the cozy flavor of cabbage rolls without the fussy rolling and stuffing. Each bowl brings 49 grams of protein and costs about $5.05 a serving (at everyday cost). One skillet, 14 servings, and none of the babysitting.
cost_closing_html: About $5.05 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls gives you 49 grams of protein and about 560 calories.
upsell_html: Cheap, filling, and loaded with veggies, this is meal prep that earns its spot in the fridge. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Buy the 6 lb ground beef value pack and let the cheap cabbage do the rest of the stretching.
A whole head of green cabbage runs under a dollar a pound and shreds down to a huge pile, so it is one of the best deals in the store.
Canned crushed tomatoes are fine here, so grab the store brand cans and skip the name-brand markup.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it goes, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook until they soften.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and the chopped cabbage, then cover and simmer until the cabbage wilts down, about 15 minutes.
Fold in the cooked rice and let it warm through so it soaks up the sauce.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve it up in bowls.

head.description: A high-protein Eastern European meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 560 calories and 49 grams of protein for roughly $5.05 each (at everyday cost).
